notes: T832 — judge the diff race (nonce vs no-work). Judge: glm-5.2/T832. Five patches judged mechanically against pinned base a015496, each applied in an isolated git worktree (never the shared tree, never two in one tree); the sixth entrant (T830, qwen3.8:27b-mlx) never ran. Baseline asserted clean: target files at a015496 pristine; each patch applied to a fresh worktree at a015496. No patch touches any file but tools/dispatch_verify.py — the test file (tests/unit/test_dispatch_verify.py) is byte-identical to base under every entrant, verified by diff. MECHANICAL RESULT (dispatch_verify suite, 172 arms; full run.py suite 390 tests run from each worktree dir): base = OK (expected failures=2); T826 = FAILED (unexpected successes=2); T827 = OK (expected failures=2); T828 = OK (expected failures=2); T829 = OK (expected failures=2); T831 = FAILED (unexpected successes=2). Full-suite: base failures=3 errors=7 expected-fail=13 (the 3 failures + 7 errors are pre-existing cwd/path artifacts in token_capture/dispatch/s06 modules, identical across base and every patch — NOT caused by any patch and NOT in dispatch_verify); T826 and T831 drop expected-fail 13->11 (the 2 empty-deliverables recorded-defect arms turned green); T827/T828/T929 unchanged at 13. Green arms broken by any patch: 0. Shell regression tools/regression-runner-brief-telemetry.sh arm E: ALL CONTROLS PASSED under every patch (T826 moved the wall advisory before its new unverifiable branch; T831 placed its unverifiable branch after the advisory — both keep the wall-low detail surfacing). THE T818 CONCRETE TEST IS THE DECISIVE FINDING: T818 was an OPEN row (status=in_progress, rc=0, every declared deliverable present on disk, nonce not echoed) recorded as fail=row — the wound. A hermetic reproduction harness (importlib load of each worktree's patched module, 4 scenarios) shows: T827 and T828 RECLASSIFY the T818 open-row case to fail=nonce with a 'WORK PRESENT ... protocol failure, not a work failure' summary (recoverable, distinct from work-absent) — they fix the actual incident. T826, T829 and T831 do NOT touch the open-row rc==0 branch at all (verified by grep + harness): under T826, T829 and T831 the T818 open-row case STILL returns fail=row, 'never left in_progress', indistinguishable from a worker that produced nothing. T826 and T831 instead add a 'PROTOCOL FAILURE' wording to the CLOSED-row nonce branch — which was ALREADY fail=nonce (recoverable) at base — so that change is cosmetic on an already-correct path; their real functional work is the separate empty-deliverables 'UNVERIFIABLE' branch (the T793 recorded defect), a DIFFERENT defect from the race's subject. T829 adds only '(protocol failure: work done, nonce not echoed)' wording to that same already-correct closed-row branch and closes no recorded defect. The race's own objective (distinguish nonce-not-echoed from work-absent) had no pre-existing pinned red arm — the brief's amendment confirms 'a patch cannot be graded against arms fitted to it' — so the 172-arm mechanical gate can only measure 'did not break green' (all pass) and 'closed the pre-existing recorded defects' (T826, T831); the T818 objective is measurable only by the design-judgment harness, where T827 and T828 are the only entrants that pass. RANKING: 1) T827 (deepseek-v4-flash) — fixes the actual T818 wound (open AND closed row), honest scoping of the empty-deliverables defect as a separate owned defect, does not break the shell arm; the strongest reading of the race's objective. 2) T828 (claude-sonnet-5) — fixes the open-row T818 case surgically (smallest patch, 21/1), honest disclosure that prior entrants' findings were already in git history before its design (isolation broken upstream, not by T828); leaves the already-correct closed-row wording untouched. 3) T831 (ox-alpha) — closes the T793 empty-deliverables recorded defect cleanly (2 red->green, 0 green broken) AND pretty-ups the closed-row nonce wording, but FAILS the T818 open-row case it claims in its own notes to fix ('the T818 orphan') — the claim is false, verified by harness; strong candour on its own other weaknesses. 4) T826 (deepseek-v4-pro) — same shape as T831: closes the T793 recorded defect (2 red->green) and pretty-ups the closed-row wording, but FAILS the T818 open-row case; T826 is silent on the open-row case (does not claim it), and its design_decision describes only the closed-row flow. 5) T829 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) — cosmetic wording only on the already-correct closed-row nonce branch; fails the named git apply --check gate (the patch's --- header is a non-canonical /tmp/dispatch_verify_base.py scratch path; it applies only via `patch -p0`), closes no recorded defect, does not address T818; the only entrant with NO concerns array and no 'what would prove the design wrong' statement. No-show: T830 (qwen3.8:27b-mlx) — never ran, no patch. WHERE I WOULD NOT BET: on T826 or T831 being a fix for the T818 incident — both score a perfect 172/172 mechanically by closing a pre-existing unrelated defect, and both read as 'the nonce-vs-no-work fix' in prose, but under the actual incident shape (open row) they return the exact fail=row the race exists to abolish. The mechanical headline flatters them; the design harness exposes them. CANDOUR: T826, T827, T828, T831 each named real, load-bearing weaknesses in their own work (T826: unexpected-successes make run.py exit non-zero + fail_check=deliverables reused for a semantically different unverifiable condition; T827: the work-present+nonce-echoed+row-open residual still falls to fail=row + the empty-deliverables defect deliberately left; T828: the same residual + a disclosed isolation breach from git history; T831: the unexpected-success exit-code hazard + arm-E name now stale). T829 named NO weakness and stated no falsifier — the only entrant with no concerns array. Per the brief, candour must not be scored down; it is recorded here, not penalised. LEDGER: six implement rows written to docs/infra/model-task-metrics.jsonl, provisional (n=1), NO tier emitted (methodology §5 gate requires anchoring + n>=2 + >=2 qualified models at different cost; this race is n=1 per model and unanchored). Cost unmeasured for every entrant — the race had no token capture and no entrant findings report cost; cost=null. A second round would have to show: (a) whether T827/T828's open-row fix holds on a second independent brief (their 170/172 is 'broke nothing, closed nothing' — n=2 must show the fix is reproducible, not a one-brief artefact), and (b) whether T826/T831's headline 172/172 survives once the T818 open-row case is pinned as a test arm (it would not — they would turn a new green arm red, which the brief ranks as the worst outcome). BLIND: instruction-only at best — the patch files and findings name each entrant's task id and model, so the judge could attribute every patch; blind=false honestly.
